title: McKinney 1031 Exchange Sourcing
name: McKinney 1031 Exchange Sourcing
metaDescription: 1031 exchange sourcing for McKinney's downtown square retail, Craig Ranch medical office, and airport-adjacent aviation property, run to the 45-day deadline.

sections.html: McKinney has grown north along US-75 and State Highway 121 faster than its commercial stock has fully caught up, which means an exchanger sourcing replacement property here finds a mix of long-established assets and product still proving itself. The historic downtown square holds adaptive-reuse retail and restaurant space around the courthouse, Craig Ranch has built out a medical office and corporate campus north of downtown, and McKinney National Airport supports a smaller but real base of aviation-related commercial property. Self-storage and neighborhood retail elsewhere in the city have generally tracked the pace of new rooftops rather than run ahead of it. Fewer of these assets have traded multiple times compared with an older Dallas suburb, so comparable sales data can be thinner than an exchanger might expect, and pricing a property here sometimes requires leaning on nearby Collin County suburbs for reference points rather than pure McKinney-only sales history.

sections.heading: Downtown McKinney Square Adaptive Reuse
sections.html: The buildings ringing the historic courthouse square have largely been repositioned into restaurant, boutique retail, and small-office space, and many of these structures predate modern building codes, which means mechanical, electrical, and fire-suppression upgrades are common line items on a recent capital improvement history. A buyer should request whatever permit history exists for a specific building before assuming current systems meet code for the intended use, since a change in tenant type inside one of these older structures can trigger a more extensive upgrade requirement than a newer building would face.

sections.heading: Craig Ranch Medical Office and Corporate Campus
sections.html: Craig Ranch has developed a medical office and corporate campus base north of downtown, anchored in part by hospital-system-affiliated outpatient facilities, and this product generally carries longer lease terms and more institutional underwriting than the older downtown stock. A buyer should confirm whether a given building's anchor tenant carries a hospital system affiliation, since that relationship can support renewal probability beyond what the lease term alone indicates, and should review parking ratio relative to patient volume for any outpatient-facing building.

sections.heading: Aviation Property Near McKinney National Airport
sections.html:
McKinney National Airport supports a smaller commercial category serving corporate and general aviation, including hangar space and fixed-base-operator facilities, and this asset class carries diligence requirements that look nothing like a standard office or retail acquisition. Demand at this airport has grown alongside the broader business-aviation activity moving north out of the Dallas core. A diligence file for airport-adjacent aviation replacement property typically includes:

  • Airport authority ground lease terms and remaining lease years
  • FBO or sublease rights tied to the hangar or facility
  • Fuel storage environmental compliance review, where applicable
  • Hangar door clearance and taxiway access confirmation
  • Title and easement review specific to the airport authority's land
  • Tenant estoppel certificate

Confirming remaining ground lease years is especially important with airport authority land, since financing terms and resale value both depend heavily on how much lease term remains.

sections.heading: Identification Timing in a Submarket With Thinner Trading History
sections.html: Because McKinney has less trading history than an older, more built-out suburb, especially for newer product tied to residential growth like self-storage or neighborhood retail, exchangers sourcing here often name a downtown or Craig Ranch candidate with more established comparable sales alongside a newer, growth-corridor property under the three-property rule, keeping the better-documented candidate as a fallback if comparable data on the newer asset proves too thin to support the purchase price within the 45-day window.

sections.heading: Qualified Intermediary and Lender Coordination for Aviation and Specialty Property
sections.html: Lenders unfamiliar with airport authority ground leases sometimes need more time to underwrite an aviation-property acquisition than a conventional office or retail deal, so identifying a lender with specific experience in this asset class before formal identification helps keep the transaction on pace for the 180-day closing deadline. The qualified intermediary holds exchange proceeds throughout this process and releases them at closing; this describes process and coordination only, and McKinney exchangers should confirm tax treatment with their own advisor.

faqs.q: What should I check before identifying a building on the downtown McKinney square?
faqs.a: Request the permit history for the specific building, since many predate modern building codes and a change in tenant type can trigger a more extensive mechanical or fire-suppression upgrade than a newer building would require.

faqs.q: Does a Craig Ranch medical office tenant's hospital affiliation matter for underwriting?
faqs.a: Yes. A hospital system affiliation can support renewal probability beyond what the lease term alone shows, so confirming that relationship is worth the extra diligence step.

faqs.q: What is unusual about diligence on aviation property near McKinney National Airport?
faqs.a: Ground lease terms with the airport authority, FBO or sublease rights, and fuel storage environmental compliance all require review beyond a standard office or retail checklist, and remaining ground lease years affect both financing and resale value.

faqs.q: Why is comparable sales data thinner in McKinney than in an older Dallas suburb?
faqs.a: Much of the city's growth-corridor product, including self-storage and neighborhood retail, is newer and has traded fewer times, so identifying a better-documented downtown or Craig Ranch candidate as a fallback is a common approach.

faqs.q: Do all lenders finance airport authority ground-lease property the same way?
faqs.a: No. Lenders unfamiliar with this structure often need more underwriting time, so identifying a lender with specific experience before formal identification helps. The qualified intermediary still holds and directs exchange funds; this is process description only, and investors should confirm tax treatment with their own advisor.
